newsitem.title: USA: Anaheim, Calif., to vote on Walt Disney expansion.
newsitem.headline: Anaheim, Calif., to vote on Walt Disney expansion.

text.p: Elected officials in Anaheim, Calif., were expected Tuesday to approve Walt Disney Co.'s $1.4 billion expansion of its Disneyland resort.
At a meeting in Anaheim, Tuesday night, the city council will consider the development plan for the project.

The city council will also consider a financial agreement that would provide $546 million in infrastructure improvements to the area around the proposed theme park and for improvements to the city's convention facilities.
To help fund these improvements, the city would issue revenue bonds, backed in part by Disney.
"This proposed agreement secures the city's economic future," said Anaheim Mayor Tom Daly. "Not to move forward would be jeopardising our tourism industry, which is our economic base."
Disney officials estimated that the new project would create 14,500 new jobs in southern California, including 8,100 in Anaheim alone.

Disney said it intends to build the theme park, called "Disney's California Adventure," next to its famed Disneyland complex. Construction of the second theme park was expected to begin in early 1997 with completion planned by the year 2001.

The first-phase expansion plans would include 750 new hotel rooms within a deluxe resort hotel, and the Disneyland Centre, a retail, dining and entertainment centre that will cater to guests and convention visitors.
As part of the plan under consideration Tuesday, $546 million would be spent for local improvements, including a $150 million expansion of the city's convention centre.

"This project is the best, most cost-effective way to deliver the necessary enhancements to the tourism district surrounding Disneyland," Daly said. "We believe the expansion will increase tourism and help avoid stagnation."
In August, Walt Disney won approval from the city's planning commission to build its $1.4 billion project.
